subject: biology
title: DNA and the genome
key_idea: Genetic material is **DNA**, a polymer of two strands twisted into a double helix. DNA is packed into chromosomes in the nucleus. A **gene** is a short section of DNA that codes for one protein. The **genome** is all of an organism's genetic material.

blocks.text: The genetic material in the nucleus of a cell is a chemical called DNA. This section covers its shape and what it is made of.

items.meaning: Deoxyribonucleic acid. The chemical that genetic material is made of.
A long molecule made of many repeating smaller units. In DNA the units are nucleotides.
The shape of DNA: two strands twisted around each other.
One of four compounds on a DNA strand: A, C, G and T.

items: DNA is a long **polymer** made of repeating nucleotides.
A DNA molecule has **two strands**, twisted into a **double helix**.
Each strand has a backbone of sugars and phosphates.
Each nucleotide carries one base: A, C, G or T.

blocks.text: How the two strands are held together

items: The strands are linked by pairs of **complementary bases**.
A always pairs with T. C always pairs with G.
The bases in each pair are joined by weak **hydrogen bonds**.
DNA is a polymer of two strands forming a double helix.
Bases pair A with T and C with G, joined by weak hydrogen bonds.
The sugar and phosphate backbone is on the outside of each strand.

blocks.text: DNA is organised into chromosomes, genes and a genome. Tap each part to see how they fit together.

diagram.alt: Tap each part of the genetic material to learn what it is.
diagram.prompt: From the nucleus to the genome

parts.name: Nucleus
parts.detail: The part of the cell that contains the genetic material.

parts.name: Chromosome
parts.detail: A structure in the nucleus that contains DNA. A human body cell has 46.

parts.name: DNA
parts.detail: A polymer made of two strands twisted into a double helix.

parts.name: Gene
parts.detail: A small section of DNA on a chromosome. It codes for a particular sequence of amino acids, which makes a specific protein.

parts.name: Base
parts.detail: A, C, G or T. Complementary bases link the two strands: A with T and C with G.

parts.name: Genome
parts.detail: The entire genetic material of an organism.

items: A gene is a small section of DNA on a chromosome.
Each gene codes for a particular sequence of **amino acids**.
That sequence makes a specific **protein**.
A group of three bases codes for one amino acid.
Chromosomes in the nucleus contain DNA.
A gene codes for a sequence of amino acids, which makes a specific protein.
The genome is all the genetic material of an organism.

blocks.text: The whole human genome has now been studied. Knowing it is important for medicine and for our understanding of the past.

items: Genes linked to different types of disease can be found. This can lead to better prevention, diagnosis and treatment.
Inherited disorders can be better understood and treated, for example by gene therapy.
Embryo screening can help make sure a faulty allele is not passed on.
Human migration patterns from the past can be traced. One example is how aboriginal people spread across Australia.
DNA analysis shows a person which alleles they have. Relatives can be told if they have inherited an affected gene.
Studying the human genome helps find genes linked to disease.
It helps with inherited disorders and with tracing human migration.

checks.q: Describe the structure of a DNA molecule.
checks.a: A polymer made of two strands twisted around each other: a double helix. The strands are linked by complementary base pairs.

checks.q: What is meant by the term genome?
checks.a: All the genetic material (DNA or genes) of an organism.

checks.q: Complete the sentences. A gene codes for a particular sequence of ___. This sequence makes a specific ___.

worked_example.question:
Scientists working on the 'Human Genome Project' have now mapped the entire genetic code of humans.

Explain one way this could be important for people in the future.
answer_points: It can identify genes linked to certain diseases (such as cancer or diabetes).
So it can lead to better prevention or treatment of that disease.
worked_example.tip: Pick one route and give the reason. Two other routes score too: genes causing inherited disorders (so IVF or gene therapy may prevent children being born with them), or tracing human migration to understand ancient history.

worked_example.question:
Part of a DNA molecule has this code on one strand:

T  T  G  A  T  T  G  C  G  T  A  A

Write the code for the complementary DNA strand.
answer_points: A A C T A A C G C A T T
worked_example.tip: One mark if all the As and Ts in the top line are correctly paired, and one if all the Cs and Gs are correctly paired.
